title: Reasons to stay natural: PEDs will not solve your insecurities
summary: NH argues that the deepest benefit of natural lifting is psychological: building a body you're content with, by your own effort, gives lasting confidence. PEDs act as a crutch that makes your physique dependent on a substance, tend to amplify existing insecurities, and lead users to escalate doses chasing a peace they never reach.

claims.claim: Many men start lifting out of insecurity because their body doesn't match the image they want, or they believe others judge them for being skinny or fat.
Lifting is sculpting a body you feel comfortable in; the confidence that results is a double effect: others find the physique attractive and you exude contentment.
Being 'alpha' really just means being happy with who you are; the best outcome of lifting is feeling at home in your body instead of seeing it as an enemy.

Contentment looks different per person (a bigger body at higher bodyfat, or a ripped six-pack); being content isn't the end, but further progress then comes from well-being instead of fighting demons.
With PEDs, part of you always knows the body wasn't built by you alone; a natural physique is yours for life and can be rebuilt naturally.
On PEDs you become subservient to the substance; even 'just TRT' users have shut down natural hormone production and their muscle depends on the dose.
PEDs are a crutch that pushes insecurities away temporarily; without the crutch they return, and in NH's experience with users they often get worse.
'Roid rage' has some truth: exogenous male hormones increase energy and aggression, but they don't make people bad; they amplify existing insecurities.
Size won't fix an insecurity like being short; you could be 400 lb and it wouldn't work. You must first be content with who you are, then improve naturally.
Insecure PED users usually escalate: when insecurity returns they take more, chasing 'a bit bigger, a bit leaner', while altering brain chemistry so inner peace stays out of reach.
Feeling insecure is normal, especially for teenagers; lifting gives direction and helps in every aspect of life even if you don't pursue it seriously.
The most valuable part of lifting is mental: proving to yourself you can change your body and your life. All you need is hard work and patience; teenagers who jump on PEDs throw this away.
Kids copy confident-looking enhanced men, but you only see them on camera; many bodybuilders die young, go down dark paths or have legal trouble, which NH links to never mastering insecurity.
Learn to control insecurity and emotions early so you don't wake up in your 40s still lacking emotional control.
